history.text:
Love the app you made. Re: lovable, though, this is the tension I’m feeling. After I saw this, I found the website and tried Lovable for a grassroots business map, and the prototype preview it made was honestly amazing - much better than what we have now. But then the hard questions came up: who is going to maintain it, who pays monthly, where does the data live/stored and who is going to be responsible for it, and what happens if the company changes terms or disappears - go out of business or merged? AI can make creation of an app easy, but small community groups still need tools they can care for, understand, and leave easily if necessary. In other words, we need more help with stewardship / maintenance of the app after it was created, not just creation, and data protection in public domain and not controlled by Big Tech.

It seems like there are options to export on GitHub but this kind of things requires technical knowledge and I don’t have time to learn all of that and that’s where this is still not yet useful to ordinary folks. That’s the part I hope we keep talking about.

Love the app you made. Re: lovable, though, this is the tension I’m feeling. But then the hard questions came up: who is going to maintain it, who pays monthly, where does the data live/stored and who is going to be responsible for it, and what happens if the company changes terms or disappears - go out of business or merged? AI can make creation of an app easy, but small community groups still need tools they can care for, understand, and leave easily if necessary. In other words, we need more help with stewardship / maintenance of the app after it was created, not just creation, and data protection in public domain and not controlled by Big Tech.

It seems like there are options to export on GitHub but this kind of things requires technical knowledge and I don’t have time to learn all of that and that’s where this is still not yet useful to ordinary folks. That’s the part I hope we keep talking about.

I think the big problem is this: having two factions of humanity would almost absolutely lead to those two factions becoming antagonistic. The best protection we have against forced biotech/ tracking tech is passing “right to refuse” laws. This would be the right to not have a cell phone, or to be reachable after hours, the right to not be tracked or recorded by providers who offer necessary services (utilites like your phone or internet or your car). The right to not have your data aggregated by 3rd parties, to build profiles about you that can be used to exploit or extort. These companies are building as fast as they can, knowing that policymakers cannot respond fast enough to stop them. 

All that to say, we have to get specific about the protections we want, and fast.
